THE  family  of  Thorpe  took  its  name  from  a  village  called 
Thorpe,  near  Chertfey  in  Surry,  where  it  was  originally 
feated  in  the  reign  of  king  Edward  I.  and  had  considerable 
poffeflions  there,  and  in  other  parts  of  that  county.  In 
the  1 2th  and  13th  years  of  king  Richard  the  Second,  Johannes  de 
Thorpe  was  returned  to  parliament  as  one  of  the  knights  of  the  fhire 
for  Surry 1 ;  and  before  that  time,  two  perfons  of  the  name  of  Thorpe 
were  monks  of  Chertfey  abbey,  as  appears  by  their  wills  ftill  extant 
in  the  prerogative  office  of  the  archbifhop  of  Canterbury.  Among 
the  names  of  the  gentlemen  of  Surry,  as  returned  by  the  commif- 
fioners  anno  1 2  Hen.  VI. a  we  find  Johannes  Thorpe  de  Thorpe,  ar- 
miger,  together  with  John  Bowet  de  Bokham  Magna,  armiger,  whofe 
family  ended  in  an  heirefs,  married  to  John  Thorpe  of  Cudworth, 
in  the  parifh  of  Newdigate,  in  that  county3,  and  of  Gibfaven,  in  the 
parifh  of  Worth,  in  the  adjacent  county  of  SufTex«;  where,  as  well 
as  at  Horn  and  Ifield,  he  had  large  PofTeftions.  The  male  line  of 
this  branch  of  the  family  becoming  likewife  extinct,  the  before  men- 
tioned eftates  vefted  in  an  heirefs,  Ann  Thorpe,  who  carried  the  fame 
with  her  in  marriage  to  William  Saxby  of  Lingfield,  in  the  county 
of  Surry,  efquire. 

From  another  branch  of  the  Thorpes  of  Chertfey  defcended  Ed- 
ward Thorpe  of  Rolvynden,  in  the  county  of  Kent,  who  dying  in 
the  year  1493,  was  fucceeded  in  his  eflate  by  his  fon  Bartholomew 
Thorpe  of  Lamberhurft,  in  the  fame  county.  He  dying  in  the  year 
1545,  was  fucceeded  in  his  eftate  by  his  fon  Thomas  Thorpe  ;  who  left 
iffue  three  fons,  William,  Richard,  and  Bartholomew  Thorpe.  Wil- 
liam, the  eldeft  fon,  greatly  increafed  his  eftate  by  marrying  Ann,  the 
widow  of  William  Lifteny,  of  Wefterham  in  Kent,  at  which  place  he 
feated  himfelf,  and  died  in  the  year  161 5,  leaving  Thomas  Thorpe 
his  eldeft  fon  and  heir.

now  fliut  out  from  the  church.    The  walls  of  it  yet  remain  overgrown  with  bufhes. 

In  the  following  churches  are  no  memorials:  Afherft,  Bidborough,  Capell,  and 
Lidling  a  chapel  of  eafe  to  Gillingham.
